messages:
Sam Park: Quick heads-up — CI on eval-runner started failing for q4-small quantized model bring-up. Seeing per-sample trace outputs shifted by one index; metrics look inflated for some runs.
Anya Rodriguez: Details? full stack or logs?
Sam Park: short log:
```
INFO eval_runner: wrote trace batch 42 (samples: 100..199)
WARN uploader: manifest mismatch for run=2024-04-q4-small: expected 100 entries, found 99
```
Sam Park: sample ids in the uploaded artifacts don't match outputs — looks like async flush / worker reorder. reproducible locally when running with --quantize and --async-kv
Mike Chen: I saw something similar last week with quantized KV cache worker. it reuses buffers and the final flush could drop last entry if buffer.size%batch_size != 0
Jen Li: CI failing tests are the dashboard regressions — the per-route BLEU jumped because we attributed sample N to sample N-1
Anya Rodriguez: Can we add sequence_id in each trace row and assert monotonic on ingest? Also need a CI test to run with low-batch-size to trigger edge case
Sam Park: proposed patch: attach 'seq_id' (int64), 'batch_idx' (int), 'quant_flags' to each sample; uploader to validate contiguous seq_ids and fail fast. PR incoming: will post link
Mike Chen: 👍 also need migration script to reindex recent runs that are affected (last 24h) — otherwise dashboards show bad comparisons
Sam Park: I opened a short-lived revert on the dashboard ingest rule to hide affected runs until we fix
ci-bot: Build 1892 failed: eval-runner-test timeout
oliver-bot: Deployed canary of uploader with seq_id checks to staging
Jen Li: action items: 1) add seq_id and CI test (Anya), 2) uploader validation + failfast (Mike), 3) migration for recent runs (Sam), 4) dashboard filter (Me/Jen)
Anya Rodriguez: I'll whip up a unit test that simulates out-of-order buffer flush and asserts detection
Mike Chen: I'll work on uploader PR and add metrics for dropped_entries
Sam Park: timeline: aim to have PRs by EOD, rollout to prod tomorrow AM, migration script after PRs land
Jen Li: thanks. also add retention note — if we reupload corrected artifacts, ensure we don't violate 7-day retention for ephemeral evals. maybe write corrected artifacts as new run_id with suffix '-fixed'
Sam Park: good point. we'll tag fixed runs and update dashboards to prefer '-fixed' where present
Anya Rodriguez: FYI, quantization flagged: only q4-small is affected so far
Mike Chen: sounds plausible — quant backend uses async I/O path
Sam Park: ok, will post PR links here shortly
Jen Li: :thumbsup:
